issues.what: The head, visor and face plate still don't match the concept, which asks for a sickle-shaped dawnglass visor over a slim carved chalk face plate with ink eye recesses, and no beige mannequin face. Improvements: the visor is now a band with a beak hook and temple horns, the vertical gouges are gone, the portrait speckle is gone, and the mouth and chin show beside the hook. Still wrong: (a) the face is a smooth beige-ivory oval with only faint tan contour lines, so it reads as a mannequin or egg; (b) the ink eye recesses can't be read in any shipped render; (c) at portrait yaw 28 the visor reads as a tall lavender shield running to the chin with a thin rim, not the concept's thick-rimmed curved sickle.
issues.evidence: Scratch crops head_cmp.png (concept vs portrait), portrait_face.png (portrait.png crop 180,150-330,360: beige oval, thin mouth line, no carving planes), splash_head.png (splash.png crop 850,70-1250,470: the face looking up reads as a blank mannequin under a sunglass-like band), three_head.png (three_rishal.png crop 1200,600-1500,900: white egg face and mannequin-like temple knob). In the builder's face2.png the eye recesses are faint blurry blobs behind the glass. Concept head crop (400,100)-(720,420) has bold white-and-ink carved planes, a visible chin and a thick pale-blue visor frame.
issues.fix: Rebuild the face plate as carved chalk: whiter (#D8D6D0, not warm ivory), with real carved planes in the geometry or strong ink-and-lit-lip paint for brow, cheekbone, nasal ridge, mouth and chin. Make the ink almond recesses read through the glass (darker, sharper, larger). Give the visor the concept's thick pale-blue frame (about 1.5-2 cm), and cut the glass back so it covers the eyes and upper cheek only, with the beak as the single part reaching below the chin. Check portrait, splash and three.js close-up side by side with the concept crop.

issues.what: The task says no neon crest, but the accent was moved, not removed. The fins are pale now. However, the new rear-rise vanes are large saturated emissive slabs running along both flanks of the crest to its tail. From the game camera front they make a blue mohawk on the crest; from behind they are two blue patches either side of it; in the portrait and splash they show as a neon headband plus a neon blade behind the crest. They cover about 13 % of the back's top band. The builder flagged this for a decision.
issues.evidence: _fit/lineup_fr2_final.png panel 1 (crop scratch lineup_pol_vs_fr2.png: blue strips either side of the white crest), builder head9.png and _fit/look_head_fr2.png (top and back views: two big blue wings along the crest), portrait.png (blue vane behind the crest, neon brow band), rishal_fr2_b5_back.png. Brief §7 budgets a ridge fin of about 30x6 cm (1.8 %). The concept has no emissive on the crest.
issues.fix: Have the brief owner rule on §7 before any more geometry work. Any fix must keep accentOk (at least 1 % per facing). Two options: (1) let the swept fins carry the team colour again, but as thin glass blades well apart from the crest so they don't read as crest trim, and drop the vanes; or (2) keep a much smaller rear rise, a narrow lip under the crest's root that stops at the crown, and pass the back facing with a short accent keel on the nape plate. Reject anything that puts emissive along the crest's length.

issues.what: The albedo's crown is creeping over the brief's L* 86 line. Earlier passes reported base p99 78-79 with 0 % above 86; now p99 is 88.5. On screen, gt90 is only 0.07-2.7 %.
issues.evidence: My decode of rishal_base (UV-covered texels): 3.69 % of texels above 86, 1.42 % above 88, 0.03 % above 90. By area, 2.7 % of the body overall and 22 % of the top tenth of the height (helm and crest tops, caps, lens) are above 86. Map: scratch atlas_gt86_cov.png.
issues.fix: Cap the baked top light or VALUE_KNEE at about L* 85 on the helm, crest and cap tops. That costs about 1 L* of top-25, and there is 10 L* of headroom over the target.
